rich_summary: Sage Valmiki asks the divine sage Narada whether a perfect man exists—one who embodies virtue, courage, wisdom, truth, and compassion. Narada answers by recounting the life of Rama of the Ikshvaku line, describing his noble qualities and the great events of his life. He summarizes Rama’s exile due to Queen Kaikeyi’s demand, the loyal companionship of Sita and Lakshmana, and King Dasaratha’s death. In the forest Rama slays demons and later forms an alliance with the monkey king Sugriva after killing Bali. The search for Sita leads Hanuman to leap to Lanka, find her, and burn the city. Rama builds a bridge across the sea, defeats Ravana, proves Sita’s purity through the fire ordeal, and returns to rule Ayodhya in a just and prosperous reign—establishing the ideal of righteous kingship.

highlight_spans.why: Opening invocation introducing Valmiki and Narada and framing the quest for the ideal human being.
Narada’s declaration of Rama as the rare hero possessing the extraordinary virtues Valmiki seeks.
The pivotal moment when Ravana abducts Sita after the deceptive lure that draws Rama and Lakshmana away.
Hanuman’s leap across the ocean and discovery of Sita in Lanka—one of the epic’s most iconic mythic episodes.
Rama’s army crossing the ocean bridge and the climactic battle culminating in Ravana’s defeat.

top_scenes.scene_text: Ravana seizes Sita and lifts her into the sky in his chariot while the wounded vulture Jatayu falls below after trying to save her.
Hanuman launches across the vast ocean toward the golden city of Lanka, the wind whipping around him as the island fortress rises from the sea.
Rama’s vast monkey army storms Lanka as Rama confronts Ravana in a blazing battlefield of arrows, chariots, and shattered towers.
